business_patterns.top_pattern: VA acute leukemia inpatient outlier in TANF Standard
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: VA / TANF Standard / ACUTE HOSPITAL / IP Med/Surg
business_patterns.pattern_details: A single inpatient acute leukemia case is driving the VA increase in TANF Standard acute hospital spend. The pattern is highly concentrated and looks like a rare catastrophic case rather than broad utilization growth. Because the clinical and operational views point to the same event, the right action is a case-level review of coding, medical necessity, and reimbursement together.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: One case is large enough to materially move results, so confirming its accuracy matters before any broader utilization or payment response.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Complete a case-level review of the VA acute leukemia admission covering diagnosis and procedure coding, level of care, and contract payment accuracy.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is concentrated in a single low-baseline case with missing procedure detail, so the claim should be validated before broader action.
evidence_summary: One VA TANF Standard acute hospital case added about $1.9M.
Paid per admit increased by about $1.9M with 1 additional claim.
Acute Leukemia with MCC drove nearly all of the positive change in this slice.
Diagnosis C9201 appeared with no recorded procedure detail in the clinical view.

business_patterns.top_pattern: NJ rare IP Med/Surg case cluster
business_patterns.pattern_details: NJ shows a narrow IP Med/Surg cost increase tied to low-volume K5650 cases rather than a broad inpatient trend. The impact is concentrated in Peritoneal Adhesiolysis with CC and appears to reflect a small cluster of higher-cost cases. This should be handled as targeted clinical validation, not a broad utilization intervention.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Small case clusters can distort trend results and trigger the wrong policy response if they are treated like systemic inpatient growth.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Route the NJ K5650 inpatient cases for case-level clinical review and confirm coding completeness before changing utilization policy.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The pattern is low volume, highly concentrated, and includes missing procedure detail in the clinical view.
evidence_summary: NJ K5650 IP Med/Surg cases added about $50K across 3 claims.
Peritoneal Adhesiolysis with CC was the main driver.
Average paid per claim increased by about $17K.
Procedure detail was blank in the clinical view.

business_patterns.top_pattern: NJ Family Care acute hospital payment spike
business_patterns.pattern_details: Within NJ Family Care, acute hospital spend rose from a very small base and was concentrated in a single higher-cost case. The pattern reflects both claim growth and higher paid amount per case, but it is not broad enough to indicate a market-wide hospital trend. The business lever is claim-level reimbursement and admission review.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is actionable as a focused payment and appropriateness check, but too narrow to support broad contract or UM changes on its own.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review the NJ Family Care acute hospital claim for pricing accuracy and admission appropriateness, then determine whether any facility-specific follow-up is needed.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase comes from a single low-baseline claim with concentrated impact.
evidence_summary: One NJ Family Care acute hospital claim added about $30K.
Paid per admit increased by about $30K with 1 additional claim.
This single case represented just over half of the positive change in the operational slice.

business_patterns.top_pattern: AR MINIMED DME mapping issue across clinical and LTSS views
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: AR / MINIMED DISTRIBUTION CORP / OP HH/DME and LTSS Non Dual
business_patterns.pattern_details: AR shows a small but recurring provider-specific signal tied to MINIMED DISTRIBUTION CORP, with activity appearing in both OP HH/DME and LTSS Non Dual views. The common issue is classification quality: facility and clinical fields are not mapped cleanly enough to support confident utilization or reimbursement action. This is a gating validation pattern first, with provider follow-up only after mapping is corrected.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Provider-specific spend signals can be misread when claims are sitting in not-mapped buckets, leading to the wrong operational response.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Validate provider, facility, and clinical mapping for MINIMED DME claims in AR and correct claim classification before any utilization or payment intervention.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Both AR views contain not-mapped or unmapped classification flags tied to the same provider.
evidence_summary: MINIMED DISTRIBUTION CORP drove a recurring AR signal across OP HH/DME and LTSS Non Dual views.
Clinical DME claims tied to E109 and E1165 contributed about $3K.
A separate LTSS Non Dual view showed 5 additional claims and about $2K in Not Mapped facility activity.
Both views include unmapped or not-mapped classification issues.

business_patterns.top_pattern: IN MINIMED LTSS not-mapped provider signal
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: IN / LTSS Non Dual / MINIMED DISTRIBUTION CORP
business_patterns.pattern_details: IN shows a small provider-specific LTSS signal tied to MINIMED DISTRIBUTION CORP, but the activity sits in a Not Mapped facility bucket. That makes this primarily a classification and payment-setup validation issue rather than a clean provider economics trend. The immediate business lever is data correction, then provider or payment review if the signal remains.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Provider-specific actions are unreliable when the underlying claims are not assigned to a valid facility classification.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Validate facility mapping and payment setup for MINIMED LTSS claims in IN before any network or utilization action.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The signal is low volume and concentrated in a Not Mapped facility category.
evidence_summary: MINIMED DISTRIBUTION CORP in IN LTSS Non Dual added about $2K.
The increase involved 3 additional claims.
The activity sits in a Not Mapped facility bucket, making this a validation-first issue.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA isolated acute hospital emergence in TANF Standard
business_patterns.pattern_details: CA shows an isolated acute hospital increase from a very small base, concentrated in a single Peritoneal Adhesiolysis with CC case. This looks like a one-off emergence rather than a broad product or hospital utilization issue. The right response is claim-level review, not a wider market action.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Small one-claim events should be filtered from broader trend responses unless they repeat or validate as a payment issue.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Perform a one-claim review for CA TANF Standard acute hospital pricing and case classification; if valid, treat it as an isolated event.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The signal is concentrated in one low-baseline claim.
evidence_summary: One CA TANF Standard acute hospital claim added about $11K.
Paid per admit increased by about $11K with 1 additional claim.
The driver was Peritoneal Adhesiolysis with CC, indicating an isolated case rather than a broad trend.

business_patterns.top_pattern: MD isolated acute hospital emergence in ABD Non Dual
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: MD / ABD Non Dual / ACUTE HOSPITAL
business_patterns.pattern_details: MD also shows a small, concentrated acute hospital increase from a very low base. The impact is tied to a single Peritoneal Adhesiolysis with CC case, suggesting isolated emergence rather than sustained utilization or reimbursement pressure. Business response should stay narrow unless this pattern repeats.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This type of small-base spike can create noise in trend reporting if it is not separated from recurring drivers.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Perform a one-claim review for MD ABD Non Dual acute hospital pricing and case classification, then watch only for repeat occurrence.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The signal is concentrated in one low-baseline claim.
evidence_summary: One MD ABD Non Dual acute hospital claim added about $9K.
Paid per admit increased by about $9K with 1 additional claim.
The driver was Peritoneal Adhesiolysis with CC, consistent with an isolated case.

executive_summary.headline: The main story is one very large VA inpatient leukemia outlier, a smaller NJ inpatient/acute hospital case cluster, and provider-specific not-mapped DME activity tied to MINIMED in AR and IN.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: Most of the observed increase is not broad-based utilization growth. It is concentrated in rare or single-case inpatient events and in small provider-specific claims that sit in not-mapped buckets. Business leaders should prioritize case-level validation on the large VA event, targeted NJ claim review, and data-quality correction on MINIMED activity before broader authorization, UM, or network actions.
recommended_focus_order: Validate and adjudicate the VA acute leukemia outlier first.
Complete targeted NJ inpatient and Family Care acute hospital claim reviews next.
Fix MINIMED not-mapped classification issues in AR and IN before provider or utilization action.

NJ clinical and operational groups were kept separate because they support different business levers: clinical case review versus product/facility payment review.
